title: Held-out training path is doubly broken: CE reduced before mask, and 6 anchors vs labels 0-9
description: train_correspondence uses ce=nn.CrossEntropyLoss() (default reduction='mean', line 287). In the held-out config, run_one_seed builds corr_ho with num_anchors=6 (line 575) so model.anchors is (6, anchor_dim) and logits_vis/logits_aud have 6 columns (315-316), but the training set from build_paired_feature_dataset contains labels 0-9 (loops range(10), lines 251,261). ce(6-col logits, target=9) raises RuntimeError 'Target out of bounds', so held-out training crashes every seed. Even if it did not crash, the mask is applied AFTER the mean reduction: loss is already a scalar, so loss=loss*mask.float() broadcasts to (B,) and loss.sum()/mask.sum() collapses back to the same scalar, making the held-out exclusion a no-op. main() wraps run_one_seed in try/except (669-672), so the crash is swallowed and NO per-seed CSV rows are ever written; the script's central 'held-out 6-9 retrieval' deliverable never runs. The paper's held-out-retrieval-at-chance numbers cannot have been produced by this code path.
evidence: line 287 ce=nn.CrossEntropyLoss(); lines 318-324 loss_vis=ce(logits_vis,labels); loss=loss_vis+loss_aud; if len(held_out_classes)>0: loss=loss*mask.float(); loss=loss.sum()/(mask.sum().clamp(min=1)); line 575 corr_ho=...num_anchors=6; lines 251,261 build_paired_feature_dataset loops range(10) so labels are 0-9
fix: Filter logits and labels by the keep-mask BEFORE calling ce (or set reduction='none' and average only the kept per-sample losses). The held-out config must train on 0-5 samples only so targets are in [0,5] and match the 6 anchors; masking the data also removes the target-out-of-bounds crash.

title: Invalid Mantel permutation null (permutes vectorized triangle, not objects)
description: _mantel_test permutes the vectorized upper triangle yv directly (line 161 perm = rng.permutation(len(yv)); yp = yv[perm]) and correlates. A valid Mantel test permutes the n underlying objects (rows AND columns of one RDM together) and recomputes the upper triangle; permuting the 45 distance entries independently breaks the distance-matrix dependency structure and yields an invalid permutation p-value. The observed r (line 157) is fine, but the reported vision_audio_rdm_p is not a valid Mantel p. This diagnostic underpins the 'RDMs uncorrelated (Mantel r, p)' claim.
evidence: lines 159-167 rng=np.random.default_rng(seed); for _ in range(permutations): perm=rng.permutation(len(yv)); yp=yv[perm]; rp=corrcoef(xv,yp); p_value=(count+1)/(permutations+1); called at line 197 on the 10x10 RDMs
fix: Permute the n=10 objects: draw a permutation of indices, apply it symmetrically to one RDM (rdm[np.ix_(perm,perm)]), then re-extract the upper triangle and correlate.

title: _spearman uses no-ties rho formula on tie-averaged ranks with normal-approx p
description: _spearman computes rho via the shortcut 1 - 6*sum(d^2)/(n*(n^2-1)) (line 136), which is only exact when there are no ties, yet it feeds tie-averaged ranks from _rankdata; with ties the rho is slightly biased. The p-value is a normal approximation to the t-distribution (lines 141-143). For n=45 pairs this is roughly OK but not exact; if it enters the paper it should be labeled approximate.

fix: Use the Pearson-of-ranks definition (tie-consistent) for rho, or scipy.stats.spearmanr; mark p as approximate if kept.

title: Checkpoint-skip staleness trap on T1/T2/T3 (silent stale results)
